title: Sequoia Health integration call notes - PoC / infra asks
content:
Call date: 2026-04-15
Attendees: Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood infra), Dr. Maya Reddy (Sequoia Health - Clinical), Alex Ortiz (Sequoia - Eng), Sofia Martinez (Redwood Solutions)
Duration: 45m

High-level objective
- Sequoia Health wants a PoC to power chart summarization + question-answering over EHR notes for internal clinician sprints. Must be PHI-safe (no external logging of identifiable data) and run in a private deployment (VPC/on-prem discussed).

Background / context
- Use case: clinicians upload daily notes (avg 400-700 tokens, peak 2k). They want: 1) concise daily summary, 2) quick Q&A over recent notes, 3) extract structured meds/allergies.
- Customers already evaluate a couple of LLMs in-house; main asks are data residency, audit logs, and low latency for interactive use (~500ms ideally, up to 2s acceptable).

Customer constraints & requirements (captured during call)
- Data residency: patient data MUST stay in their VPC. No log egress to hosted Redwood control plane unless explicitly accepted and encrypted.
- Compliance: HIPAA; they need KMS/HSM integration and audit trail for every inference.
- Throughput: initial PoC ~ 5 concurrent clinicians, burst to 25. Production projection: 200 concurrent sessions within 6-12 months (depends on adoption).
- Latency: median 600ms token generation target for chat/QA flows; summarization can be async (30s SLA ok).
- Sequence lengths: median 600 tokens, 95th pct 1800 tokens.
- Cost sensitivity: they want guidance on model/quantization tradeoffs. Prioritize accuracy for clinical safety but cost must be justified.

Integration notes (technical)
- Preferred deployment: Redwood Private in their AWS account (VPC peering) or on-premises appliance - they prefer VPC first.
- Auth: Sequoia uses Okta; need SAML/OIDC integration for user auth + RBAC in Console.
- Data flow: clinicians' uploads should go into S3 (customer bucket). Redwood runtime should pull via cross-account role; recommend using signed short-lived URLs for upload and then processing inside Private deployment (no S3 copy to Redwood-managed buckets).
- Key management: Must integrate with their AWS KMS. They will not allow keys to leave account.
- Logging: audit events must be streamed to their CloudWatch/ELK; Redwood must support per-request audit metadata (user-id, patient-id tokenized, model-id, latency, response hash).

Model / runtime considerations
- They want to start with a larger open model (instruction-tuned) for summarization accuracy. Explore quantized 16->8-bit paths to save cost but validate hallucination risk.
- Need embeddings for semantic search of notes; index in their infra (no external embedding storage).
- KV cache: for Q&A, session affinity and prefix caching will help latency. Discussed autoscaling policy for dedicated pools and predictable throughput.

Gotchas / red flags called out
- PHI + control plane: major blocker if control plane sees unredacted patient data. Need clear docs on where PII appears in telemetry and opt-outs.
- Okta integration timeline could delay PoC if we require SAML setup on their side. Offer a short-lived API-key fallback for PoC (dev/test) with clear limitations and no production acceptance.
- Long context lengths (up to 2k) increase memory/GPU footprint; we should propose batching/streaming strategies and possibly chunked summarization.

Open questions (need answers before scope finalization)
- Will Sequoia accept Redwood Private control plane with metadata only, or do they require full private control plane (no external metadata)?
- Which AWS region/account will host the Private deployment? Need region for capacity planning and instance selection.
- Are there required certifications beyond HIPAA (e.g., HITRUST)?
- Which model family do they prefer for PoC (we suggested Llama 3 / mix-of-checkpoints) - ask clinical team if they have prior validation set.

PoC proposal (tentative)
- Phase 0 (1 week): onboarding + security review. Get sandbox account, cross-account role, KMS policy, minimal SAML test OR API-key fallback.
- Phase 1 (2-3 weeks): Deploy Redwood Private in their AWS account (small footprint: 2 GPU nodes for inference + 1 control plane vm). Integrate KMS + audit streaming.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): Basic PoC features: ingest sample notes, generate summaries, run Q&A with embeddings stored in their infra. Collect quality metrics vs. clinician-provided gold.
- Phase 3 (2-4 weeks): Load testing, autoscaling policy, cost projection, and rollout plan for 200 concurrent sessions.

Action items & owners
- Priya: Draft PoC SOW + security appendix and share by 2026-04-18.
- Liam: Prelim infra sizing + cost estimate for region us-east-1 by 2026-04-20.
- Alex (Sequoia): Provide sample dataset (anonymized) and clinician acceptance criteria by 2026-04-22.
- Sofia: Prepare demo prompts and evaluation checklist; confirm model candidates by 2026-04-19.

Notes / informal (scratchpad)
- Clinician cares a lot about "no hallucinated meds" - include a policy to fall back to "I don't know" on low-confidence extractions.
- Consider a hybrid approach: run high-sensitivity checks with a smaller deterministic extractor for meds/allergies, then use LLM to fill in summaries.
- If they insist on on-prem, need to loop in SRE and release-eng early (packaging + install runbook).

Next meeting: tentatively 2026-04-23 to review SOW and infra estimate.

Quick links (for follow-ups):
- Internal: https://confluence.internal/redwood/pocts/sequoia-2026 (draft SOW will live here)
- Jira: INTG-8421 (PoC epic)

End of notes.
